subject: pri-info-td
title: (R)PRI.INFO.TD.------TRS.
description: Diagram in the Extended Functionalism (II) section (EXT.F(II)-6), opening Braxton's argument about creative music's seventies trajectory and decentralization. (R)PRI-VT-TD (the reality of primary vibrational tendencies) is crossed with TRS (transition). The diagram poses what real primary vibrational tendencies look like when crossed with transition in the seventies' integrated context — where the AACM, post-Ayler, and St. Louis movements are converging. ALT-D (alternative definitions) → PRI-VT-TD; POL-DYM (political dynamics) → PRI-VT-TD. CR-INFO-DY (circular information dynamics) → TRS; ALT-F (alternative functionalism) → TRS. ALT-F also branches to CRTF-D (cross-transfer definitions) → ACC-DY (accelerated dynamics), to PROG-CONT (progressional continuance), and to LANG (language). Structural argument: real primary vibrational tendencies are fed by both alternative definitions and political dynamics — meaning the seventies integration required both definitional reframing *and* political-dynamics work. Transition is fed by circular information dynamics (the recursive flow of meaning) and alternative functionalism. Alternative functionalism then fans into four sibling outputs: cross-transfer definitions (which produces accelerated dynamics), progressional continuance, language, and transition itself. The diagram thus diagrams the integrated structural conditions of the seventies: real primary vibrational tendencies and transition are co-active, with alternative functionalism as the central productive node — but alternative functionalism's four-fold output (definitional, dynamic, progressional, linguistic) means the seventies decentralization is structurally fragile, requiring all four lines to remain active.
